summary: This article explains how Ibn Battuta of Tangier left home for Hajj in 1325, kept traveling for almost 30 years across Africa and Asia, and left behind the Rihla, a book historians still use.
introduce: Write Inform, Persuade, and Entertain on the board and give a one-line example of each. Tell students to decide, while reading “Ibn Battuta: A Traveler of the World”, which purpose the writer had and to find one sentence that proves it.

keyTerms.def: a journey to a holy place
a person who has studied a subject for a long time and knows a lot about it
a title for a ruler in some Muslim lands in the past

challengeTerms.def: made up of many different kinds
to say words aloud so that someone else can write them down

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that traveling teaches you more than reading about places in books? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Describe Ibn Battuta's journey in order, from when he left home to when his book was written.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review pilgrimage, scholar, and sultan, and let weak readers underline sentences that inform and circle any that persuade.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses diverse, perilous, and dictate to explain the writer's purpose and how the details support it.
